title: Uniform codimension bound for normalization jets
statement:
Let $k$ be algebraically closed [def-weil-field], $r\ge2$, and let $D\subset\mathbf P^{r-1}_k$ be a nonempty reduced closed subscheme of pure dimension one [def-pc-reduced-scheme, def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-pure-dimension]. Put $L=\mathcal O_D(1)$ [def-pc-projective-space-twist] and let $\nu:\coprod_{i=1}^s C_i\to D$ be the disjoint union of the normalizations of its reduced irreducible components [def-sc-normalization]. The $C_i$ are smooth proper connected curves. Put $L_i=\nu^*L|_{C_i}$ and $e_i=\deg L_i>0$ [def-pc-degree-line-bundle]. Fix finite sets $S_i$ of distinct closed points of $C_i$. For integers $m\ge1$ and $n_q\ge0$ satisfying $\sum_{q\in S_i}n_q\le me_i$ for every $i$, let $U_{m,n}\subset H^0(D,L^{\otimes m})$ consist of sections whose pullbacks have order at least $n_q$ at every $q$ [def-sc-ringed-space-module-cohomology, def-sc-divisor]. An order is measured in the discrete valuation local ring after a local trivialization of the line bundle; the zero germ has infinite order. There is a real constant $C\ge0$, depending on $D,L$ and the sets $S_i$ but not on $m$ or the tuple $n$, such that
$$\dim_k H^0(D,L^{\otimes m})-\dim_k U_{m,n}\ \ge\ \sum_{i=1}^s\sum_{q\in S_i}n_q-C.$$
The sets $S_i$ may be empty and several points in a given $S_i$ may map to the same point of $D$.

proof.text:
Put $\widetilde D=\coprod_i C_i$. The given embedding makes $D$ projective, hence proper by [lem-pc-projective-proper]. Apply [lem-trf-reduced-curve-normalization-genus] to this nonempty proper reduced pure one-dimensional scheme: the component list is finite, $
u$ is finite, and its components are smooth proper connected curves, without requiring $D$ connected. By [lem-trf-normalization-singular-skyscraper] there is an exact sequence $0	o\mathcal O_D	o
u_*\mathcal O_{\widetilde D}	o Q	o0$ with $Q$ coherent and supported on finitely many closed points. Define $\delta=\dim_kH^0(D,Q)$, finite by [lem-pc-chi-zero-dim-support]. For each $i$ let $Z_i=
u(C_i)$ be the corresponding irreducible component of $D$ with its reduced induced structure; since $D$ has pure dimension one, $Z_i$ is an integral closed one-dimensional subscheme of $\mathbf P^{r-1}_k$, and $C_i	o Z_i$ is its normalization. Both $\mathcal O_D(1)$ and $\mathcal O_{Z_i}(1)$ are restrictions of $\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^{r-1}}(1)$ (same gluing data on the standard opens), so $L_i$ is the pullback of $\mathcal O_{Z_i}(1)$ to the normalization of $Z_i$, and [lem-sfb-integral-curve-span-degree-rigidity] gives that $e_i=\deg L_i$ is a positive integer, as the statement asserts.

proof.text:
For every $m\ge1$, tensor the sequence of step 1 by $L^{\otimes m}$. This is exact: on any open trivializing the line it is the original sequence, and exactness is local. On such an open multiplication by the chosen frame identifies $L^{\otimes m}\otimes
u_*\mathcal O_{\widetilde D}$ with $
u_*
u^*L^{\otimes m}$; on overlaps both identifications change by multiplication by the same transition unit, so they glue. Thus sections give an injection $ho_m:H_m=H^0(D,L^{\otimes m})\hookrightarrow T_m= igoplus_iH^0(C_i,L_i^{\otimes m})$, and $T_m/ho_m(H_m)$ injects into $H^0(D,Q\otimes L^{\otimes m})$, by the left-exact part of [pqf-def-cohomology]. The equality between sections upstairs and sections of a direct image is its definition, and sections of a finite disjoint union are the component tuples by the sheaf axiom. By [lem-pc-chi-zero-dim-support], $\dim_kH^0(D,Q\otimes L^{\otimes m})=\delta$. Hence $\dim H_m\ge\dim T_m-\delta$, uniformly in $m$.

Write $g_i=\dim_kH^1(C_i,\mathcal O_{C_i})$. By [lem-sc-global-functions], $H^0(C_i,\mathcal O_{C_i})=k$. Coherent cohomology on each proper curve is finite by [lem-pc-coherent-hi] and is zero in degrees above one by [lem-sc-noetherian-cohomology-above-dimension]; its Noetherian and integral hypotheses follow from [lem-sc-smooth-connected-curve-local-rings]. Consequently $\chi(C_i,\mathcal O_{C_i})=1-g_i$. Degree is the difference of Euler characteristics by [def-pc-degree-line-bundle], and tensor additivity [lem-trf-curve-degree-tensor-additive], iterated $m$ times, gives $\deg(L_i^{\otimes m})=me_i$. Thus $h^0(C_i,L_i^{\otimes m})=me_i+1-g_i+h^1(C_i,L_i^{\otimes m})\ge me_i+1-g_i$. In particular all components of $T_m$ are finite-dimensional, and step 2 then also shows $H_m$ finite-dimensional.

proof.text: For each $i$, put $B_i=\sum_{q\in S_i}n_q[q]$ and $N_i=\deg B_i=\sum_{q\in S_i}n_q$. Apply [lem-sfb-smooth-curve-section-degree-cap] with $A=L_i$, its integer $m$ equal to the present $m$, its integer $q=1$, and effective divisor $B_i$. It identifies the vanishing subspace $W_{i,m,n}$ with $H^0(C_i,L_i^{\otimes m}(-B_i))$ and bounds its dimension by $\max\{me_i-N_i+1,0\}=me_i-N_i+1$, since the hypothesis of the item is $N_i\le me_i$. The zero divisor is explicitly allowed by that node. Set $W_{m,n}=\bigoplus_iW_{i,m,n}\subseteq T_m$; then $\dim W_{m,n}\le\sum_i(me_i-N_i+1)$.

source.place: Tag 0CCS, lemma-grd-inequalities; tensor/divisor degrees: varieties.tex Tags 0AYX and 0AYY

proof.text: By the definition of $U_{m,n}$, the injection $\rho_m$ identifies it with $\rho_m(H_m)\cap W_{m,n}$. Therefore $\dim U_{m,n}\le\dim W_{m,n}$. Combining steps 2--4 gives $\dim H_m-\dim U_{m,n}\ge\sum_i(me_i+1-g_i)-\delta-\sum_i(me_i-N_i+1)=\sum_iN_i-(\delta+\sum_i g_i)$. Take the nonnegative integer $\delta+\sum_i g_i$ as the required real $C$. It is independent of $m,n$ and even of the sets $S_i$. Empty marking sets give $B_i=0$, while points with the same image in $D$ remain distinct in their respective normalization divisors, so neither allowed case changes the argument.

The estimate is true with C = delta + sum g_i. I tested a smooth conic (the bound is an equality), a nodal cubic (codimension 1 >= 2 - 1, which shows C >= delta is needed), empty S_i, n = 0 and N_i = m e_i. Step 1: the hypotheses of the genus lemma and the skyscraper lemma hold, and the skyscraper lemma's componentwise normalization is the same nu as the item's. Step 2: the twisted sequence and frame identification are elementary, pqf-def-cohomology gives left exactness, and chi-zero-dim-support (3) and (2) give h0(Q tensor L^m) = delta. Step 3: global-functions, coherent-hi and above-dimension vanishing apply (Noetherian from local-rings), chi(O) = 1 - g, and 0AYX additivity gives deg L^m = m e with the same chi degree convention, so h0 >= m e + 1 - g. Step 4: the section-degree cap (already reviewed PASS) with q=1 and B=B_i gives the vanishing space and h0 <= m e - N + 1. Step 5: U = rho^-1(W), and the arithmetic is correct. One gap: the statement asserts e_i = deg L_i > 0 and no step proved it. FIX: step 1 now applies lem-sfb-integral-curve-span-degree-rigidity (same unit, unsplit, no proof deps, so no cycle) to Z_i = nu(C_i), an integral closed 1-dimensional subscheme of P^{r-1} with O_D(1)|Z_i = O_Zi(1). Its statement says e is a positive integer. The node is added to the step's uses and to proof_deps; nothing else changed. Tool uses are generic and accepted.
